title: PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement results — a pay-as-bid average price for new PJM supply, not a clearing price; re-dated from 2026-12-02 after FERC suspended the procurement (PJM refiled 2026-10-29)
source: EST: RE-DERIVED 2026-11-02 (was 2026-12-02). The original tariff arithmetic (open + 3 weeks + 6 weeks) no longer applies: FERC's 2026-09-29 order in ER26-3380-000 / EL26-108-000 accepted the RBP for filing but SUSPENDED it for five months, 'effective February 28, 2027, subject to refund', set paper-hearing procedures, and 'strongly encouraged' a new FPA section 205 filing (order PDF fetched direct from pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercOrders/9154/20260929-er26-3380-000.pdf 2026-11-02, HTTP 200, text-extracted locally; and insidelines.pjm.com/ferc-accepts-pjm-reliability-backstop-proposal/, PJM: 'the RBP process will not begin on Sept. 30'). The window never opened 2026-09-30, so results cannot land 2026-12-02. NEWS: PJM refiled a revised RBP on 2026-10-29 proposing launch 2027-03-01, bid window closing 2027-03-28, final target 2027-04-28 and results posted 2027-05-10 (mgrid.org/2026/10/31/..., plus an APPA and PA Environment Digest summary relayed by search); no PJM or FERC primary document for the refiling was reached, so 2027-05-10 is a proposed date conditional on FERC accepting the refiling, not a posted one. Original derivation, retained for the record: EST: derived by tariff arithmetic from PJM's own FERC filing in docket ER26-3380-000 (accession 20260731-5214, filed 2026-07-31), fetched direct from pjm.com/pjmfiles/directory/etariff/FercDockets/9806/20260731-er26-3380-000.pdf on 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200) and text-extracted locally. The filing publishes NO absolute results date — it publishes a RELATIVE schedule (Proposed Tariff, Attachment DD, section 18.4): the offer submission window 'is planned to open upon Commission acceptance of this submittal, close three weeks after, and the subsequent clearing and selection process will take place thereafter and conclude six weeks following the closing of the offer submission window.' PJM states it 'requests that the Commission issue an order on this filing and make this proposal effective by no later than September 29, 2026' and that 'Upon Commission acceptance of this filing without modification, PJM intends to commence the RBP on September 30, 2026.' Open 2026-09-30 + 3 weeks = 2026-10-21 close; + 6 weeks = 2026-12-02. Both press-reported dates fall exactly out of that arithmetic (utilitydive.com/news/pjm-backstop-capacity-auction-ferc-data-centers/826792/, 'bid window September 30 - October 21', 'results due by December 2'). Filed estimate for a stronger reason than the taxonomy: the date is EXPRESSLY CONDITIONAL and slips day-for-day with the FERC order. PJM's own footnote — 'The RBP procurement window will open if and when a Commission order [accepts the] framework... absent significant revisions or developments' — and its Part V — 'Should the Commission require modifications to the proposed RBP as detailed in this filing, PJM may need to delay the commencement of the RBP beyond September 30, 2026' — make the whole chain contingent. As of 2026-09-08 no FERC order accepting ER26-3380 was found on any search run, and the PJM Independent Market Monitor filed a protest (monitoringanalytics.com/filings/2026/IMM_Protest_Docket_No_ER26-3380_20260821.pdf, fetched direct 2026-09-08, HTTP 200) asking the Commission to REJECT the filing outright as 'unjust and unreasonable'. pjm.com/markets-and-operations/rpm publishes no RBP schedule, so the confirmed `PJM:` prefix (pjm.com auction schedule) does not apply. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: Canonical file written 2026-09-08 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md ('When your own event was proposed by others'). Supersedes proposals/pjm-reliability-backstop-results-2026-12-02.from-pjm-capacity-auction-2026-12.json, which discovered this event during the 2026-09-08 pjm-capacity-auction-2026-12 adjacency sweep; that proposal stays where it is and goes inert. TITLE AND FRAMING AMENDED against the proposal on primary-source evidence the proposal did not have. The proposal called this 'the first PJM capacity print able to clear above the $325 collar cap'. PJM's filing shows there is no clearing price to speak of: the RBP is PAY-AS-BID ('a pay-as-bid structure, unlike a single clearing price structure, relies on individual clearing prices rather than a single clearing price'), the $555/MW-day UCAP figure is a MW-WEIGHTED-AVERAGE budget constraint on levelized procurement cost across all Delivery Years — not a hard cap on any individual offer — and $555 is precisely Point 1 of the VRR curve for the 2028/29 BRA, i.e. the uncollared cap the collar suppressed, not a new higher willingness to pay. The published number will be an average of accepted asks levelized over a 15-year term with commercial-operation dates out to 2032-06-01; it is not comparable to a one-year RPM clearing price. Impact medium and symbols empty on the proposing ledger's grounds, re-verified: none of the nine tracked names is an IPP, the exposed names (VST/CEG/TLN/NRG) live in docs/research/ai-energy-constraint.md rather than on the tracked roster, and no house playbook is keyed to a capacity procurement. Estimate — nothing here licenses a date-keyed entry. Full assessment: docs/research/events/pjm-reliability-backstop-results-2026-12-02.md RE-DATED 2026-11-02 by this event's pulse (docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md kill switch: re-derive, never patch in place): date 2026-12-02 -> 2027-05-10 (estimate). The id keeps its original slug because the filename is the id (--validate); read the id's date as historical. The 2026-12-02 results date is dead, and with it the sequencing premise in the original title ('landing ~2 weeks before the 2029/30 BRA'): PJM's own filing puts the BRA opening 2026-12-09, so the RBP now reports after that auction, not before it. 2027-05-10 sits beyond assessment-cadence.json's horizon, so the event leaves the due pool until it re-enters the 60-day window; any FERC order on the refiling is a stance-relevant dated event this entry's next pulse should re-derive from.
